top: Alabama Voice Of Teachers For Education

cands.bio: Republican attorney from the Windham Springs area of Tuscaloosa County. Partner in Brinyark & Frederick and municipal judge for Centreville since 2005. Previously a municipal judge in Brent and Woodstock. Elected to Alabama House District 16 in a 2023–24 special election; seat held since January 2024.

endorsements.text: Business Council of Alabama endorsed him in the 2023 special Republican primary (per Wikipedia).
Alabama Farmers Federation endorsed him before the January 2024 special general election (per Wikipedia).

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from Brinyark on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, donor money, policing, guns or abortion. We also found no bills he sponsored, since the sponsored-legislation list on his Ballotpedia page was empty. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate surveys in 2024 or 2026, and it lists no endorsements for 2026. His school-choice position comes from a Wikipedia summary rather than a direct quote. His campaign site is undated and appears to be from the January 2024 special election. We found no news coverage of controversies, and nothing on any foreign ties.

cands.bio: Christian Martin is a Democrat and activist who graduated from Tuscaloosa High School. He ran for Alabama House District 16 in 2026 and has not held public office. His campaign focused on health care, tax policy and labor rights.

endorsements.text: He listed SDUSA and US Term Limits as endorsers in his own Ballotpedia survey response.
Ballotpedia lists him on two voter-guide recommendation lists: Tabitha's List (a Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (a Sway voting group by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, when he moved to Alabama, or any work history beyond the label "activist." He has held no public office, so there are no official actions to report. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, and no statements on homestead taxes, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable organizational endorsements beyond those listed. His platform statements come only from his own Ballotpedia survey.

score.why: Raised $3,004, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
